transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-22
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Ravi Singh, Lina Park, Owen Brooks (Redwood) - Elena Martinez, Tom Beckett, Rajiv Kaur, Priya Nair, Samir Desai (Juniper Fjord)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Maya, AE for Redwood Inference, and with me is Ravi our SE. Um, we'll run through the activation plan and capture constraints.
[00:18] Elena Martinez: Hi, thanks. We're excited to get started. We have a lot riding on latency for our chat features, but security is the bigger blocker right now.
[00:32] Ravi Singh: Great, can you say a bit about your env? Are you planning cloud VPC with peering, or on-prem?
[00:40] Tom Beckett: We'll be in GCP, private VPC, with strict egress. We need VPC peering or private link. Also we use Cloud KMS, not Hashi, so KMS integration is must.
[00:55] Maya Chen: Ok, we support GCP VPC peering and a private control plane option. For KMS we have integrations but we need to confirm key wrapping — Rajiv, is BYOK required?
[01:08] Rajiv Kaur: Yes BYOK preferred. Also audit logs must be retained 12 months and exported to our SIEM. SOC2 is fine but we need evidence on key rotation policies.
[01:22] Lina Park: Noted, we'll include retention and KMS details in the pack. Our private package supports export to SIEM via syslog or Kinesis — though sometimes the naming in docs is slightly different.
[01:37] Priya Nair: Timeline question — how quickly can we get to a pilot? We want a small beta by end of May.
[01:44] Owen Brooks: If network and keys are provisioned promptly, a two-week SE-run pilot is realistic. We usually do a sandbox deployment, model pinning, and a smoke test for latency and throughput.
[01:58] Samir Desai: For the pilot we need to test both low-latency chat path and bulk embedding jobs. Can the same infra handle both?
[02:08] Ravi Singh: Yes but we'd recommend separate pool configs — dedicated low-latency pool and a batched embed worker. We'll detail batching and quantization suggestions in the runbook.
[02:22] Maya Chen: Quick note — on cost controls we can set routing policies to fallback to a cheaper model for non-critical calls, that might help with bulk embeddings.
[02:32] Elena Martinez: Hmm, fallback sounds useful. Will that affect response consistency? We can't have huge output drift.
[02:41] Ravi Singh: We'll set quality monitoring and per-prompt evals — automatic regression alerts. Fallbacks are model-variant based, kept behaviourally similar. We'll also surface token-level deltas.
[02:56] Tom Beckett: Network: we have a strict egress allowlist. We'll need IP ranges and a CA-signed cert for peering. Also do you support private link endpoints?
[03:08] Owen Brooks: We support both peering and private link depending on the cloud. For GCP we do VPC peering and we can supply a set of CIDR ranges and certificate requirements.
[03:22] Rajiv Kaur: About data retention — PII should never persist. Do you have a data retention / redaction flow? Also is KV cache persisted across restarts? Some runtimes persist cache to speed up warmups which is not allowed in our environment.
[03:40] Ravi Singh: We have configurable KV cache policies — can be ephemeral-only, not persisted. We also have prompt/response redaction hooks before logs are persisted. We'll include config options.
[03:54] Elena Martinez: Good. Also need SSO integration for all users — SAML and SCIM.
[04:01] Maya Chen: Yes, SAML and SCIM supported, RBAC mapping available. We'll attach a step-by-step SSO onboarding doc.
[04:09] [00:04:09] (brief cross talk)
[04:20] Priya Nair: For success metrics — what do you recommend we measure during pilot?
[04:27] Ravi Singh: Latency p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, correctness/accuracy measured via eval prompt sets, and availability/error rates. We'll provide a dashboard template.
[04:39] Maya Chen: Can we schedule a deep-dive on performance next week? We can do a 90 minute SE session and run a small synthetic benchmark.
[04:47] Tom Beckett: Yes, week of May 4th works. Prefer morning PST.
[04:53] Maya Chen: Great I'll send invites.
[05:00] Elena Martinez: Security review — we'll need to see SOC2, ISO, pen test report, and a network diagram. Also confirm whether you encrypt keys with customer-managed keys.
[05:12] Lina Park: We'll share SOC2/ISO and pen test redacted copy. CMK support is available and we can document key usage and rotation cadence.
[05:23] Rajiv Kaur: Are there any known vendor dependencies that require outbound access to third-party endpoints? We try to limit that.
[05:32] Owen Brooks: Runtime dependencies are internal; for model downloads during onboarding we use internal mirrors. No external outbound should be necessary in private deployments.
[05:44] Priya Nair: Ok, who from your side will own the pilot?
[05:48] Maya Chen: Ravi will be the SE lead for the pilot and Lina will be primary CSM. I'll own the commercial touchpoints.
[05:56] Ravi Singh: I'll prepare a pilot runbook with staging steps, model pinning, traffic shaping, and success criteria.
[06:04] Maya Chen: Quick clarify on billing for pilot — we often bill a small usage fee plus support hours. Tom, does procurement need a PO before pilot?
[06:14] Tom Beckett: For pilots procurement won't require a full contract but need an SOW and estimated costs. We'll coordinate.
[06:22] Maya Chen: Great. We'll send draft SOW and pilot pricing.
[06:29] Elena Martinez: Any red flags? From our side, main risks are KMS BYOK and the egress constraints.
[06:36] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll prioritise KMS integration docs and precise IP ranges.
[06:43] (wrap-up)
[06:46] Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood to send SOC2/ISO and KMS notes, SE to schedule May 4th perf workshop, customer to provide network diagram by 4/29, and we'll draft SOW.
[06:59] Priya Nair: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[07:02] END

Notes: There were a few transcription hiccups — some product names rendered oddly (private control plane as 'private control plain' in parts). We included timestamps at ~30s intervals but some blocks are grouped for brevity.
